title: Is Salesforce (CRM)’s Agentforce Growth Enough to Outpace F5 (FFIV)’s AI Security Momentum?
excerpt: On September 2, F5, Inc. (NASDAQ:FFIV) announced a key integration with MuleSoft, a Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) company, federating F5 AI Guardrails directly...
content_html:
On September 2, F5, Inc. (NASDAQ:FFIV) announced a key integration with MuleSoft, a Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) company, federating F5 AI Guardrails directly into MuleSoft's Agent Fabric Omni Gateway. As enterprises rapidly scale agentic AI capabilities, security teams face growing governance gaps and risks from prompt injection, data leakage, and toxic outputs. This native integration gives security and platform engineering teams centralized policy enforcement, proactive threat mitigation, and low-touch policy tuning without forcing organizations to re-architect existing infrastructure.

While the partnership strengthens both ecosystems, examining their latest financials reveals two enterprise software giants moving at distinctly different scales and growth trajectories.

Financial Performance Comparison

F5, Inc. (NASDAQ:FFIV) reported strong Q3 FY26 results, generating $865 million in revenue (up 11% year-over-year). Revenue growth was anchored by a 19% jump in product revenue, led by a 32% surge in systems revenue ($240 million). F5's bottom line remained exceptionally robust, expanding non-GAAP operating margin to 35.0% and delivering non-GAAP net income of $272 million ($4.73 per diluted share, up from $4.16).

Salesforce operated at a much larger scale in its record Q2 FY27, generating $11.3 billion in quarterly revenue (up 11% year-over-year). Growth was fueled by subscription and support revenue of $10.8 billion and expanding adoption of its Agentforce platform, whose annual recurring revenue (ARR) neared $3.9 billion. Salesforce posted a non-GAAP operating margin of 34.1%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $5.90, while raising its full-year FY27 revenue guidance to $46.1B–$46.4B.

While both companies run near-identical, highly profitable non-GAAP operating margins (~34%–35%), Salesforce leads overall financial health due to its massive free cash flow generation, cRPO backlog of $33.5 billion, and broader ecosystem dominance.

Bull and Bear Case

F5's bull case centers on growing enterprise demand for AI infrastructure security, with its high-margin hardware/software mix and specialized AI Guardrails positioning allowing it to capture niche security spending without significant overhead. However, systems revenue can be cyclical, and hardware refresh cycles could slow if enterprise IT budgets tighten.

Salesforce's bull case rests on its positioning as a leading agentic enterprise platform, supported by 210% year-over-year Agentforce ARR growth and 14% growth in cRPO, highlighting customer stickiness and expanding seat monetization. On the downside, Salesforce's top-line growth has moderated to 11% year-over-year, with momentum partly supported by incremental revenue from acquisitions such as Informatica.
